body:
Prerequisite for [[T-111]] and cheap on its own. Move every count out of its
sentence, so no user-facing string ever has to agree grammatically with a number.

## Why

Seven sites hand-roll `if (n == 1) "" else "s"`. That construct cannot be fixed by
translating strings: German needs `1 Sitzung / 2 Sitzungen`, Russian needs three
forms (1 / 2-4 / 5+), Arabic six. A translator handed "session" and "sessions" has
nowhere to put the third form.

Reformulating to `Label: N` removes the agreement requirement entirely, and doing
it at ALL seven sites means the codebase needs no plural machinery at all — no
Android `<plurals>`, no `Intl.PluralRules`, no plural-aware i18n library. T-111
then collapses to a flat key->string catalog, which is the difference between
"pick an i18n framework" and "a Map and a hook". Reformulating only SOME sites
would save nothing: one remaining site still drags in the whole mechanism.

## The rule

Bare plural in label position, count after a colon as a standalone placeholder:

- yes: `Items needing attention: 1`
- no:  `1 items need attention`

Do NOT write `Item(s)` — that is an English orthographic convention with no
equivalent elsewhere (Russian changes the stem, Arabic has six forms, Japanese
marks nothing), so a translator can't use it. A bare plural in a label does not
jar the way it does mid-sentence. Because the count becomes a lone `{n}` with no
adjacent noun, translators also get free word order: `Zu prüfen: {n}` and
`{n} zur Prüfung` are both available.

## Sites

| file | now | after |
|---|---|---|
| `android .../ui/SyncStatusBar.kt:130` | `3 items need attention` | `Items needing attention: 3` |
| `android .../notify/CollaboratorChangeNotificationPoster.kt:106` | `3 items changed` | `Changed items: 3` |
| `android .../notify/CollaboratorChangeNotificationPoster.kt:68` | `... across 2 lists` | `Changed items: 3 · Lists: 2` |
| `android .../ui/admin/AdminScreen.kt:148` | `3 sessions` | `Sessions: 3` |
| `web src/pages/AdminPage.tsx:231` | `3 sessions` | `Sessions: 3` |
| `web src/pages/ListPage.tsx:156` | `Fixed casing for 3 items in Dairy` | `Dairy — casing fixed: 3` |
| `android .../ui/settings/LastSeen.kt:27` | `3 days ago` | relative under a day, then an absolute date |
| `web src/lib/relativeTime.ts` | (already correct via Intl) | same treatment, for parity |

Note line 68 of the notification poster carries a SECOND count in the same string
("N items changed across M lists") — it needs two labels, not one.

## LastSeen, both clients

Switch to relative-under-a-day then absolute date ("Active now" / "3 hours ago" /
`Mar 14`). `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and Android's `DateFormat` localize a date for
free and it has no plurals at all. Rejected alternative: a compact duration like
`-3d4h` — `d`/`h` are themselves English abbreviations (German `T`/`Std`), so it
only looks locale-free, and it adds precision the field does not have (the server
throttles `last_seen_at` to a 15-minute window) or need (the question is "is this
session about to idle out?" against 7- and 62-day windows).

This also removes a known tension: `LastSeen.kt` hand-rolls its plural
specifically to stay testable without the Android framework (see its docstring);
an Android `<plurals>` resource would have reintroduced the `Context` dependency
it was written to avoid.

## Verification

- No `== 1` / `? "" : "s"` construct remains on any user-facing string.
- Existing tests that assert on these strings updated.
- Eyeball the SyncStatusBar banner in situ — it is the most prominent of the
  seven, and this is a real (small) shift toward terser, more label-like copy.
title: de-pluralize user-facing strings so no plural layer is ever needed
